column.note: These four are filters, not a partition: "Found by AI teammates" is a source and overlaps public/private, so they don't sum to the total.
column.title: By column

cost.note: Cost is an estimate at list price, not money paid. Gateway calls are priced at each model's rate in the gateway's price table; subscription calls are estimated at the same model's rate, though the subscription is paid monthly; models the gateway serves from our own hardware are priced from the table too, and the platform does not pay per call for them. Unpriced tokens have no rate and are not in that figure.

credits.note: Exhausted / low / unlimited are three mutually exclusive sets: unlimited means no credits were ever granted, not that they ran out. Burn rate is derived from usage records (credit grants carry no deduction history), not from balance differences. ETA is a linear extrapolation; unlimited and zero burn both show —.
credits.title: Credits burnout

empty.desc: The platform hasn't produced any data yet.
empty.title: No data yet

disk.note: Covers only this backend host's workspace directory. Remote devices and cloud machines have their own disks and are invisible here.
disk.title: Disk (this backend)

hostSlots.note: Slots held by AI teammates / all slots across the host pool.
hostSlots.title: Sandbox slots

machines.note: Rows and state distribution across four ledgers, not a container count — one-container-per-room has no transport yet.

preview.note: Process memory, cleared on restart. This process only, not platform-wide.
preview.title: Preview tunnels

health.note: This moment only — not stock, not a window. Same checks as /health/detailed.
health.title: Platform health

delivery.note: Two tiers: the first is still retried, the second is abandoned after MAX_ATTEMPTS. Collapsing them makes salvageable and hopeless look alike.
delivery.title: Delivery ledger

oauth.note: No refresh token is not the same as expired: an expired one can still be refreshed, one with no refresh token stops working for good on expiry. The expiry time is fixed when access is granted; it does not mean a recent failure.
oauth.title: OAuth authorizations

passkey.note: The denominator is all non-deleted accounts, not active ones (accounts don't record their last sign-in). Two-step verification settings live in Redis, not the database, so this reports passkeys, not 2FA coverage.
passkey.title: Passkey coverage

unavailable.githubAppMintFailureRate: GitHub App token issuing failure rate: logged only, never counted.
unavailable.githubAppPermissionGaps: GitHub App permission gaps: the granted permissions stay 10 minutes in process memory and are never stored.
unavailable.loginLockoutStockAndRate: Login lockout history: sign-in rate limits live only in Redis and keep no history.
unavailable.meteringPostFreeze: Metering posting freeze: admission fails open on transport errors and leaves no trace outside the log.
unavailable.note: Needs instrumentation. A zero here would mean checked and empty.
unavailable.title: Not observable today

machines.note: These four are stock counts from four ledgers, not live online counts — online state lives in process memory and has no column in the database.
machines.title: Machines (stock)

network.apiNote: HTTP request-body bytes in and response-body bytes out of this backend process.
network.title: Network throughput
network.uplinkNote: The default-route interface ({iface}). Uplink includes the metering proxy egress to model providers, repo sync and backups — this is the box total uplink, not just our users traffic. History is process memory and clears on restart.

perf.note: Latency per route, held in process memory: this moment only, cleared on restart, and this process only (the business API). A weekly view would have to read the request log instead.
perf.routesNote: Every registered endpoint gets a row, never-hit ones included (their call count shows an em-dash). The percentiles are exact over the last 256 samples, not lifetime.

backlog.note: Backlog is stock. A live card blocks the room from re-filing, so in-flight is not just queueing slowly.

failures.note: Counted from the reason on the platform notice each failure posts in the channel, not from run records: run records have no failure field. Refusals for lack of credits are counted separately, from the recorded refusal time.
failures.title: AI teammate run failures

host.empty: No hosts with a failure streak
host.note: Current streak only — any success deletes the row, so this cannot answer how many were quarantined last week.
host.title: Host failure streaks

needs.note: Three reasons only, a closed set (reviewer / reporter / asked).
needs.title: Needs you

stuck.note: Stuck is judged by whether the notice's code is in the stuck set, never by its text; a new code left out of the set never shows as stuck.
stuck.title: Stuck cards

pool.needsReset: the disabled ones need a manual reset
pool.note: Read from a snapshot the metering proxy writes beside the usage ledger, not from the database: the accounts behind the subscription route live only on the proxy's machine. The states are the proxy's own: cooling is a rate limit with a reset time, disabled has none and needs a manual reset. The snapshot ages, so when it is old it says when it was written.

reason.malformed: The pool snapshot is not in a shape we can read
reason.missing: The metering proxy has not written a pool snapshot yet (it may not be running)
reason.notConfigured: This deployment has no subscription metering proxy, so the pool is not on the board
reason.unknown: The pool snapshot could not be read
reason.unreadable: The pool snapshot could not be read

pool.title: Claude account pool

product.northStarNote: Counted by the time of the last decision. Revoking overwrites it, so a card accepted then revoked loses its accept moment.

rejection.note: Returned = rejected + gate red/blocked + conflict + void. A true revoke is not a return. Denominator is cards filed in the window (including still-live).
rejection.title: Where filed cards ended

unavailable.churn: Churn after credits run out: credit grants don't record when they ran out, and accounts don't record their last sign-in.
unavailable.note: No data source. Any number here would have to be invented.
unavailable.summon: Acceptance rate after mentioning the AI teammate: run records don't mark whether a mention started them, and acceptance cards don't record which run they came from, so the two can't be joined.
unavailable.title: Not computable today

reliability.note: Delivery backlog is stock, not a failure rate.
reliability.title: Delivery

spine.note: Four stations are throughput at different moments, not a funnel over one cohort. The merge station counts only cards with a PR: a card without one never gets a merge time. The machine gate is retired and not on the chain (#296).
spine.title: Delivery chain

usage.batchTitle: What the gateway totalled for this model over a stretch of time; it can cover many requests, and the ledger does not record how many.
usage.byModelNote: Bar is tokens; then money, unpriced tokens and the cache-hit rate. The first three together answer "is it the model or the billing"; a — rate means the model's calls did not record their cache.
usage.byRouteNote: The unpriced column is tokens with no rate; split by route, it shows which route they came from, and where the KPI's number comes from.
usage.byUserNote: Calls inside a project count for the person who started the AI teammate; calls outside a project count for the person who made them. This is who triggered how much, not who contributed. Runs the platform started count for nobody: {tokens} tokens, {cost} in this window.
usage.cacheNote: Cache-read tokens ÷ input tokens (input includes cache reads and writes). Only calls that recorded their cache count: each route and kind of call counts from its first recorded cache read in the window. Gateway calls written before the gateway recorded cache show 0 only because nothing was recorded, so they are left out. {tokens} input tokens in this window are left out.
usage.recentNote: The latest {n} usage rows in the window, in Beijing time. A row is not always one request: a subscription row is one request; a gateway row (marked “batch”) is what the gateway totalled for one model over a stretch of time and can cover many requests; a row from an own API key or a member's own Claude Code totals one model over one run. The ledger does not record how many requests a row covers. A — in the cache column means the row did not record its cache.
